A.reason: All five are workable conditional proposals with distinct primary mechanisms: recurring supply commitments, timed stock release, universal flexible shares, staggered arrivals and demand-responsive replenishment. Candidate 0 best directly supports predictable staple supply with modest coordination, consistent access rules and inspectable records. The buffer is usable but risks denying present requests; the other routes depend on cooperation, arrival clustering or sufficiently reliable demand records.

B.reason: All candidates are usable under their stated conditions. Candidates 0 and 5 share the recurring-commitment mechanism; delivery confirmation and commitment expiry are operational repairs, not a new mechanism. The remaining groups use timed release, flexible shares, count-triggered replenishment, loss prevention and staggered arrivals. Candidate 5 offers the strongest overall routine through explicit volunteer duties, physical-stock accounting, expiring missed commitments, shelf-capacity limits and a bounded workload. Its short trial provides only provisional evidence.

pair.reason: B5 narrowly improves on A0 by specifying how actual deliveries are distinguished from intentions and how missed commitments are cleared before further requests. It also uses the existing donor-facing schedule without assuming a separate contact channel. These concrete feasibility and inspectability gains support the same predictable-supply mechanism; neither proposal guarantees sufficient donations.
